title: Sundargaan: Songs of the Sundarbans | Studio 1947
description: Studio 1947 travelled into the Sundarbans to record its vanishing folk music, then built Sundargaan, a living digital archive where the songs of the delta's artists find a home, a voice, and fair pay.
ogTitle: Sundargaan: Songs of the Sundarbans | Studio 1947
ogDescription: Field recordings from the Sundarbans, preserved in a living digital archive, where every listen sustains the artists who carry the delta's songs.

hero.alt: A frame from the Sundargaan hero footage: the dark tidal creeks and mangroves of the Sundarbans delta

body: Where mangroves meet the restless tide, and the land quietly holds its stories, that is where Sundargaan begins. The Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove delta, is also one of its richest songbooks: Bhatiyali boat songs rowed against the current, Baul mystic airs carried on a single-string ektara, Lok Geet of harvest and household, Manasha ritual verses sung for the snake goddess. None of it is written down. It lives only in memory: and every generation that passes, part of it passes away.

Sundargaan is a living archive and cultural platform rooted in the Sundarbans, built by Studio 1947 in collaboration with The Eco Logical Foundation and Sundarbaan Unayan Bhavan. We didn't design a website first. We went to the delta, sat with the artists, and recorded the songs, then built the digital sanctuary those recordings deserved.

sections.heading: The Music That Was Never Written Down
sections.label: Why It Matters
body: The delta's oral traditions are endangered: not by neglect, but by time itself. Their bearers are aging, the young are migrating toward the cities, and the rituals, work-songs and laments that once structured life along the creeks are thinning with each season. There is no staff notation for a boatman's call. No score for a potter's song. If a voice stops singing, the song is gone.

Sundargaan's mission is to change that: rigorous field documentation of endangered folk traditions across 50+ blocks, building a comprehensive digital archive of 50,000+ songs, stories and artefacts: with the people who carry them kept at the centre, and fairly paid.

sections.heading: The Expedition: Recording the Delta
sections.label: Field Recording
body: Before a single screen was designed, Studio 1947 travelled into the Sundarbans with The Eco Logical Foundation's field team. We reached villages that sit hours beyond the last road, Kalitala, Gobindakati, Jogeshganj, Sahebkhali: where the archive's first 38 artists across 9 art forms live and sing.

The recordings themselves are the project's beating heart: a Baul master of thirty-five years coaxing a century-old tune from his ektara, a Bhatiyali singer recalling the boat-songs his grandfather rowed by, the clay-potters of Hingalganj working to a rhythm older than any clock. Every track in the archive carries the singer's name, village and craft, the recording is the gift; the archive is how it is kept.

sections.heading: Nine Genres, One Delta
sections.label: The Sound of the Sundarbans
body: Each block of the delta sings its own music. Sundargaan documents nine distinct genres: searchable, filterable, and each given its proper Bengali name and context.

cards.title: Boat Songs of the Tide
cards.body: The rowing songs of boatmen and fishermen: long, unhurried melodies shaped by the ebb and flow of the creeks.

cards.title: The Mystic Ektara
cards.body: Wandering singer-mystics of Bengal, their single-string ektara and devotional verse probing the divine in the everyday.

cards.title: Songs of the People
cards.body: The everyday music of the delta: work songs, wedding songs, songs of the field and the household.

cards.title: Ritual Verse
cards.body: Ceremonial songs for the snake goddess: among the oldest living traditions in the Sundarbans, tied to the land's dangers.

cards.title: Epic Narrative Ballads
cards.body: The great sung epics of the region: hours-long performances telling the delta's founding stories, including the Bonbibi Johuranama.

cards.title: The Baul Canon
cards.body: Songs in the lineage of Fakir Lalon Shah, carrying the Bauls' philosophy of the body, the soul, and the search for truth.

sections.heading: Press Play: Songs from the Field
sections.label: The Recordings
body: This is what the project is really about. These are the actual field recordings: the voices of the delta's artists, captured in their villages, preserved for anyone, anywhere, to hear. Every play supports the artist who sang it.

sections.label: Page by Page
body: The website is the vessel, not the story. It is built to get out of the way (warm, editorial, and fast) so that the songs, the artists and the places stay at the centre.

sections.heading: Design & Engineering for the Delta
sections.label: The Digital Sanctuary
body: The platform is a modern React single-page application: engineered for the real conditions of its audience: low-bandwidth connections, Bengali-language users, and mobile-first access from the villages themselves. The interface is fully bilingual (English / বাংলা), with a serif display face for song titles that echoes the region's printed heritage and a clean sans for reading.

The palette is drawn from the delta itself: the burnt-sienna of sun-baked clay, warm cream, and deep earth ink. Search reaches across names, songs and instruments; every record, artist and artefact can be filtered by block and genre; and the full archive can be experienced in an immersive screen.

sections.heading: The Ripple of Every Contribution
sections.label: Sustainability Model
body: Sundargaan operates on a principle of radical transparency: the money the platform generates flows back to the people who make the music. Contributions, streaming revenue and festival fees are distributed through a clear, published model, with the largest share going directly to the artists.

cards.title: Artist Share
cards.body: Direct financial support, project fees and fair wages for recordings and performances, the singers, players and artisans themselves.

cards.title: Community
cards.body: Insurance, health support and emergency funds for the artist community, and collective practice spaces that keep traditions alive.

cards.title: Operations
cards.body: Sustaining the infrastructure that records and preserves the heritage, Studio 1947 and the Eco Logical Foundation's field work.

cards.title: Security & Health
cards.body: A safety net for the bearers of the tradition: because a living archive depends on living artists.

sections.heading: Client Impact & Outcomes
sections.label: Measuring Success
list: Songs Saved From Silence: The delta's first comprehensive digital archive, field recordings of endangered genres, each credited to its singer, village and craft.
Artists at the Centre: Every track carries its artist's name and story, and the platform's revenue model routes the largest share back to them, dignity and pay, not just preservation.
Built for the Delta, Not the Metropolis: A bilingual, low-bandwidth, mobile-first platform that works in the very villages where the music was recorded.
One Voice, Two Languages: Full English / বাংলা interface honouring the community the archive exists to serve.
